scope: Selected flat-64 signed digit addition/subtraction/normalization, big_to_double, and mixed addition. Not whole-file or other arithmetic admission.
adaptations: Native unsigned double-digit carry arithmetic requires compiler 128-bit integers; native 65535-digit result ceiling is retained.
Most-significant digit comparison uses bounded indices instead of forming a pointer before the input allocation on equality.
Fallible independent domain scratch replaces ERTS heap fragments. Arithmetic finishes before possible copying collection; publication preserves heap credit and physically initialized X/Y roots.
The native compiler-overflow increment fast path shifts unsigned bits before signed conversion, avoiding negative signed-shift UB; binary64 is compile-time checked and fast-math is refused.

Generated whole plus/increment cases restore heap/stack pointers and recompute Y destinations after collection. OOM is checked before guard branching; badarith/system_limit retain native body/guard behavior.
Native big_to_double mantissa extraction and nearest/ties-even rounding; early overflow check before narrowing a large bit count.

Floating arithmetic saves the worker floating environment, installs the default IEEE environment and restores the prior environment before allocation. Environment API failure is terminal notsup, not a false guard.
Native linear digit cost at 16 words per reduction, plus actual copying collection cost, feeds the existing bounded scheduler. No hard fairness claim.
Positive catalog addition of erlang:+/2; gc_bif2 admission checks the actual catalog entry, not merely a numeric BIF identity.
Frame trim proves dropped/remaining counts and shifts Y definitions and shape facts. The original generated trim and two-register move-window cases execute unchanged.
